daysW3.title: Santo Domingo de la Calzada -> Belorado
daysW3.short_desc: A slow start and dinner with new faces
daysW3.long_desc: After many early mornings, we treated ourselves to a sleep-in and a late breakfast at our lovely hotel, Parador de Santo Domingo Bernado de Fresneda. The breakfast? Easily the best we’ve had on the Camino so far and a proper energy boost. We set off around 9:30 a.m., passing through four small villages before finally taking a coffee break in the fifth. It was a calm, easy-going day and no rush, just walking. When we arrived in Belorado, we spotted a familiar face. Eva from Varberg, waving to us from the balcony of her room. Camino reunions like that always bring a smile. We missed lunch, the Spannish kitchen had closed at 3:30 p.m. so we began searching for our accommodation for the night.  Rest Life El Santo located about 1 km outside the town center. On the way, we ran into Sharon and Glenn from Belfast, who happened to be staying at the same place. Eventually, we found a rustic rural stone house and stepped inside to find our room. The host, Fernando, prepared a shared pilgrim dinner for all the guests. There were nine of us at the table: Sharon and Glenn, Madonna (yes, that’s her real name) and her son from Brisbane, an American, and us. A slightly quirky remote but charming place and another evening full of conversations, laughter, and new connections.

daysW3.title: Belorado -> Villafranca Montes de Oca
daysW3.short_desc: A Short walk and history in the walls.
daysW3.long_desc: After two long days of walking, today’s plan was wisely kept short, just 12 kilometers, giving our tired bodies a much-needed break. The morning began with breakfast at Fernando’s, our kind host for the night. Before we left, he showed us a shortcut across his land that connected directly to the Camino trail, a thoughtful gesture that saved us both time and effort. After a morning coffee in the first village, we continued straight on to Villafranca Montes de Oca, a small town with a big historical presence. Here you’ll find Hotel San Antón Abad, originally built in the 14th century as a hospital for pilgrims. Since the 1970s, it has been transformed into a charming and comfortable hotel, complete with a restaurant, cafeteria, and bar. They offer pilgrim menus for both lunch and dinner, making it the perfect place to rest, refuel and feel the spirit of centuries of Camino history.

daysW3.title: Villafranca Montes de Oca -> Atapuerca
daysW3.short_desc: .A steep start, rocky trails, and a day that ended in Sunshine
daysW3.long_desc: .The day began early and brutally. We left our accommodation at dawn and immediately faced a tough 200-meter climb, from 960 to 1160 meters above sea level, all in just 2.7 kilometers and 50 minutes. Our bodies were completely drained before the day had even properly begun. As if the climb wasn’t enough, the trail added another challenge with rocky, uneven terrain that made every step require focus and effort. But just when we needed it most, a true Camino angel appeared, Dr. Coffee, a mobile coffee stand offering not just hot drinks and snacks, but also jazz music, energy, and a very much-needed break. By the time we arrived in Atapuerca, we were warmly welcomed at our hostel, where the host greeted us with refreshments and laundry service , a.small gestures that felt like luxury after such a demanding day. We ended the evening with a pilgrim dinner in wonderful international company with a dinner table full of laughter, stories, and shared Camino spirit. Despite the rough beginning, it turned into a day to remember with tired bodies, but full hearts.

daysW3.title: Atapuerca -> Burgos
daysW3.long_desc: Through small villages and open fields.

daysW3.title: Burgos - Rest day
daysW3.short_desc: Rest day. Sunshine, Rest, and Love in Burgos
daysW3.long_desc: What an incredible privilege it is to simply wander around Burgos on a sunny, warm Friday, with no obligations, no deadlines and just a well deserved rest day after 18 days on the Camino. What an adventure this is turning out to be. Today was all about what we needed most, sleep, shopping, a sunny lunch, sightseeing, culture, history  and yes, a proper Friday beer. The sun was shining in Burgos, with 20°C and a clear blue sky, and the city was at its finest. But the greatest privilege of all? Sharing this journey with a strong, wise, and deeply loved woman, my wife Birgitt-Marie. Walking side by side every day is both a joy and a gift. After a revitalizing coffee break, both body and mind feel ready for the next chapter; the vast and open Meseta. The Meseta is a geographical area within the region of Castilla y León and the larges region i Spain. Thecentral high plateau makes up 40% of Spain with elevation ranging from 400 m to 1000 m. What it will bring we don’t yet know. But we’re both ready.  .
